summary: st-test resolves transport spellings and pinned repository rename aliases to one pool identity. The repository's former-name key stays canonical to reuse existing warm trees. Local and file remote path case and nondefault ports stay distinct so unrelated repositories do not share a pool.

replay.detail: Local test-runner pool selection only; no graph or replay change.

schema.detail: No database or wire schema change. An optional repo-aliases.json object in the selected configuration directory maps exact normalized spellings to canonical pool identities.

rules.detail: Signing and verification rules are unchanged. Aliases are read only from the pinned accepted base. The new data file is included in the existing ci-script-tests lane definition and input paths, but is not a gate PROTECTED file.

compatibility.detail: Older bases without alias data keep their existing remote identities. The former-name pool remains warm. Non-GitHub path case, local/file paths, nondefault ports and unknown schemes such as fabric:// may change pool key once; unknown schemes now keep the whole URL. Duplicate pools remain eligible for existing global least-recently-used eviction when the pool cap is enabled and exceeded. With the cap off or not exceeded, idle duplicates can persist indefinitely. No pool migration, idle-age timer or special deletion path is added.

downtime.detail: None. Existing tree locks continue to protect active runs, including runs using former pool keys.

manual.detail: None required by this change. Pool selection leaves retired pools untouched. Operations may independently clear unlocked duplicate build output after rollout under its existing cleanup policy; the runner needs no manual migration.

recovery.detail: Revert the runner and alias data to restore previous pool selection. Existing pools remain usable until ordinary cap eviction removes their idle trees.
